key_insight: RubricsTree is a scalable, expert-aligned evaluation system that uses a hierarchical set of clinically verifiable rubrics to assess open-ended personal health agent responses more reliably than typical LLM judges.
clinical_relevance: It aims to make evaluation of AI health assistants more consistent, auditable, and clinically grounded, which is important for safer product-level deployment.
method: Built a tree of 100+ atomic Boolean rubrics from 4,000 real user health queries.
Used an iterative human-in-the-loop curation process led by an experienced physician.
Applied a context-aware router to activate only the relevant rubric subset for each query.
evidence_signal: In systematic meta-evaluation, RubricsTree outperformed a strong large-scale baseline on expert alignment and helped optimize models, producing up to ~66% relative gains on HealthBench across Gemini, GPT, and Qwen families.
watch_item: Because the rubric set is evolving and depends on expert curation, deployment may still require ongoing maintenance to keep judgments clinically aligned across new use cases.
paper_title: RubricsTree: Scalable and Evolving Open-Ended Evaluation of Personal Health Agents across Health Memory and Medical Skills
